# skill_asset_containers

The runtime contract every module runs inside: the one image, the three runners and the one resident `docker-compose.yml` writes under two anchors, the stores each service mounts and how a container addresses them, and the Makefile's `run`, `fanout` and `basket` macros that run a stage in a one-off container for one asset or for the whole basket. It also governs the host user, the init process, the one memory ceiling, the compose project's name and the host port the Makefile measures.

## Architecture

- `ASSET-CONTAINERS-ONE-IMAGE-FOR-EVERY-SERVICE`
  - Description: Every service runs the one image `liora-1m-pipeline`, built from the root `Dockerfile`; the service and its command decide the role, never a second image.
  - Scope: `docker-compose.yml`, `Dockerfile`, `Makefile`
  - Expected: `build: .` and `image: liora-1m-pipeline` on the `x-service` anchor alone, so a bare clone builds the image instead of reaching for a registry and `docker images` shows one; `make build` building it; no image per service, module or asset, and no ticker in its name.
  - Exception: none
- `ASSET-CONTAINERS-THE-IMAGE-CARRIES-THE-PINS-ALONE`
  - Description: The image is a dependency layer — the pins of `requirements.txt` on `python:3.12-slim` and no code: the code arrives through the tree mount and the state through the store mounts, so an edited module runs without a rebuild.
  - Scope: `Dockerfile`, `.dockerignore`, `docker-compose.yml`
  - Expected: `FROM python:3.12-slim`, `requirements.txt` copied and installed, `WORKDIR /app`, and no other `COPY`; `.dockerignore` excluding everything but `requirements.txt`; every service mounting the tree at `/app`.
  - Exception: none
- `ASSET-CONTAINERS-THREE-RUNNERS-AND-ONE-RESIDENT`
  - Description: The topology is three runners — `data`, `features` and `ml`, one per module of the chain, each a role and a one-off — and one resident, `dashboard`; a service is named for its runtime role, never for a ticker, a tool, an image or an author.
  - Scope: `docker-compose.yml`
  - Expected: `data`, `features` and `ml` with no `command:`, so `docker compose run --rm -T <runner>` supplies one and the container exits with its stage; `dashboard` with its own `command: python -m module_monitoring.serve` and `ports:`, kept up by `make on`; no service per asset, per stage or per tool.
  - Exception: none
- `ASSET-CONTAINERS-A-SERVICE-MOUNTS-ONLY-THE-STORES-IT-TOUCHES`
  - Description: Each service mounts the tree at `/app` and, at `/store/<content>`, the stores its stages touch and no other, read-only where it only reads; the code and those stores are all a container reaches on the host.
  - Scope: `docker-compose.yml`
  - Expected: Each store mount `./store/<content>:/store/<content>`: `data` — `raw_1m`, `assets_artifacts`, `status`; `features` — `assets_artifacts`, `status`; `ml` — `assets_artifacts`, `trials`, `status`; `dashboard` — `run_records` and `status`, both `:ro`, beside the tree mounted `.:/app:ro`; the raw store `data`'s alone and the trials store `ml`'s alone.
  - Exception: none
- `ASSET-CONTAINERS-A-CONTAINER-ADDRESSES-A-STORE-AT-ITS-MOUNT`
  - Description: A container addresses state only at its `/store/<content>` mounts, by the five `STORE_*_DIR` every service carries — the variable the name a service speaks, the mount the I/O it is granted — never through the `/app/store/<content>` the tree mount also carries.
  - Scope: `docker-compose.yml`, `module_*/**/config.py`
  - Expected: `STORE_RAW_1M_DIR`, `STORE_ASSETS_ARTIFACTS_DIR`, `STORE_TRIALS_DIR`, `STORE_RUN_RECORDS_DIR` and `STORE_STATUS_DIR` set to `/store/<content>` on the `x-store-environment` anchor and read by each `config.py` as `Path(os.environ[...])`; no store path derived from `__file__` or written as `/app/store/…`.
  - Exception: none
- `ASSET-CONTAINERS-INIT-ON-EVERY-SERVICE`
  - Description: Every service runs under an init process, because a Python process as PID 1 has no SIGTERM handler: `docker compose down` would wait out the stop timeout and kill a stage mid-write, and a one-off's init reaps whatever its stage leaves behind.
  - Scope: `docker-compose.yml`
  - Expected: `init: true` on the `x-service` anchor, inherited by all four services.
  - Exception: none
- `ASSET-CONTAINERS-ASSET-NARROWS-THE-MAKE-LINE-ALONE`
  - Description: `ASSET` narrows the make line and nothing else: no container reads it, and every stage is told its assets by `--tickers`, which has no default.
  - Scope: `Makefile`, `docker-compose.yml`, `module_*/**/*.py`
  - Expected: `TICKER_LIST` — `ASSET` if set, else `TICKERS` — feeding `fanout`; no service environment carrying `ASSET`; `build_ticker_parser()` declaring `--tickers` required; no stage module reading `ASSET`.
  - Exception: none
- `ASSET-CONTAINERS-NO-CODE-KNOWS-A-CONTAINER-NAME`
  - Description: No code depends on a container, network or project name: a stage knows `--tickers` and the `STORE_*_DIR` it reads, the server its own address in `module_monitoring/config.py`.
  - Scope: `**/*.py`, `**/*.js`
  - Expected: No `liora-<service>-1`, `liora_default` or compose service name in a Python or JavaScript file; the Makefile alone speaks docker compose.
  - Exception: none

## Naming

- `ASSET-CONTAINERS-THE-PROJECT-IS-NAMED-IN-THE-FILE`
  - Description: The compose project is named `liora` in the file, so a container is `liora-<service>-1` on every host; two checkouts on one host share the name and run one at a time, unless `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` overrides it at invocation.
  - Scope: `docker-compose.yml`
  - Expected: `name: liora` at the top of the file; containers `liora-<service>-1` and the network `liora_default`; no project name derived from the checkout's directory, none per ticker.
  - Exception: none

## Conformities

- `ASSET-CONTAINERS-TWO-ANCHORS-EVERY-SERVICE-RESPELLS-ITS-MOUNTS`
  - Description: `docker-compose.yml` writes every service under two anchors — `x-store-environment`, the store contract every service reads with the thread cap beside it, and `x-service`, what every service is — and a service respells its `volumes:` whole, because a service's key replaces the anchor's.
  - Scope: `docker-compose.yml`
  - Expected: `x-store-environment` holding the five `STORE_*_DIR` and `OMP_NUM_THREADS` (`DETERMINISM-THREAD-CAPS-FROZEN-AT-ONE`); `x-service` holding `build`, `image`, `init`, `user`, `environment: *store_environment` and the tree mount; every service `<<: *service` with its full `volumes:` list, the tree mount first.
  - Exception: none
- `ASSET-CONTAINERS-EVERY-CONTAINER-RUNS-AS-THE-HOST-USER`
  - Description: Every container runs as the host user, so nothing it writes into a store is owned by root.
  - Scope: `docker-compose.yml`, `Makefile`
  - Expected: `user: "${UID:-1000}:${GID:-1000}"` on the `x-service` anchor, fed by the Makefile's `COMPOSE_ENV` — `UID=$(shell id -u) GID=$(shell id -g)` — on every compose call, `run` included.
  - Exception: none
- `ASSET-CONTAINERS-THE-HOST-PORT-IS-MEASURED`
  - Description: `PORT` is only the host side of the dashboard's mapping, measured once per make at invocation and never hardcoded: the port the dashboard already publishes, else the first free port upward from the container's port, because another project — or a checkout run under `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` — may hold it.
  - Scope: `Makefile`, `docker-compose.yml`, `**/*.md`
  - Expected: `PORT ?=` measured by `docker compose port dashboard` and a loopback probe, then fixed by `PORT := $(PORT)`; `PORT=n` on the make line overriding it; `make on` printing the address; no document stating the host port as a number; a port taken between the look and the bind failing the start, and the next `make on` looking again.
  - Exception: none

## Workflow

- `ASSET-CONTAINERS-A-STAGE-RUNS-IN-A-ONE-OFF-CONTAINER-OF-ITS-RUNNER`
  - Description: Every stage runs in a one-off container of its module's runner and exits with it; no resident is assumed for compute, and nothing is executed inside a running container.
  - Scope: `Makefile`
  - Expected: `docker compose run --rm -T <runner> python -m <module>.<stage> --tickers …` through the `run`, `fanout` and `basket` macros — the chain's stages, the serpentine search's turn and `ml-score`, and the promotion; no `docker compose exec`; `record.py` measuring a stage from outside and knowing no container.
  - Exception: none
- `ASSET-CONTAINERS-A-STORE-EXISTS-BEFORE-IT-IS-MOUNTED`
  - Description: A bind-mounted store exists on the host before compose mounts it, because Docker would create a missing source directory as root and the host-user container could not write it.
  - Scope: `Makefile`
  - Expected: `$(STORES)` created by `mkdir -p` as an order-only prerequisite of `build`, of every stage of the three stage lists, of `features-serpentine-turn`, `ml-score`, `features-serpentine-search` and `features-serpentine-search-promote`, of `on` and of `all-record`; a new target that starts compose joining that line.
  - Exception: none
- `ASSET-CONTAINERS-ON-RAISES-THE-RESIDENT-OFF-TAKES-EVERYTHING-DOWN`
  - Description: `make on` builds the image if needed, raises the one resident and prints and opens the page's address; `make off` stops and removes every container of the project.
  - Scope: `Makefile`
  - Expected: `on: build`, then `docker compose up -d dashboard` and `http://127.0.0.1:$(PORT)/` printed and opened; `off:` running `docker compose down`; the dashboard with no target of its own.
  - Exception: none

## FileLayout

- `ASSET-CONTAINERS-ONE-COMPOSE-FILE`
  - Description: One `docker-compose.yml` at the root carries the whole topology, every service visible in it.
  - Scope: `docker-compose.yml`, `Makefile`
  - Expected: The `COMPOSE` and `run` macros with no `-f` and no `COMPOSE_FILE`; no second compose file and no override file anywhere in the tree.
  - Exception: none

## Scalability

- `ASSET-CONTAINERS-FANOUT-PER-ASSET-BASKET-ONCE`
  - Description: A per-asset stage runs through `fanout`, one container per ticker, at most `JOBS` side by side; a basket-wide stage runs through `basket`, once for the whole basket, which `ASSET` never narrows.
  - Scope: `Makefile`
  - Expected: `fanout` — `TICKER_LIST` into `xargs -P <width>`, one `run` with `--tickers <TICKER>` each, `data-ingest` at width 1 and every other per-asset stage at `$(JOBS)`; `basket` — one `run` with `--tickers $(TICKERS_CSV)`: the three status stages, and the download as one container per venue, a venue's rate limit being budgeted per process.
  - Exception: none

## Complexity

- `ASSET-CONTAINERS-NO-RESTART-POLICY-NO-HEALTHCHECK`
  - Description: No service carries a restart policy or a healthcheck: a failure is reported by its exit, never hidden by a restart.
  - Scope: `docker-compose.yml`
  - Expected: No `restart:` and no `healthcheck:` on any service or anchor; a stage's non-zero exit failing its `make` target.
  - Exception: none

## Performance

- `ASSET-CONTAINERS-THE-ML-RUNNER-ALONE-CARRIES-A-MEMORY-CEILING`
  - Description: The `ml` runner alone carries a memory ceiling, set above `DUCKDB_MEMORY_LIMIT` to bound a runaway allocation of the hyper-parameter search and XGBoost outside DuckDB; `data` and `features` allocate nothing outside DuckDB's own ceiling, the resident computes nothing, and concurrency is bounded by `JOBS` alone.
  - Scope: `docker-compose.yml`
  - Expected: `deploy.resources.limits.memory` on the `ml` service and on no other; no `mem_limit`, no reservation, no CPU quota; no ceiling on the anchor.
  - Exception: none
